items.title: Tom Varner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 13, 2025
items.q: The interviewer shares a quote from Karl Berger, and the interviewee (Tom Varner) responds by discussing the content of the quote ('I like Karl's quote...'), indicating he is aware of Berger's views but no personal interaction or professional collaboration is described in the text.

ctx.x: I had a couple quotes here about free improv. And I wanted to share them with you, see if you have a reaction. The first one is from Karl Berger, who said to me, “More freedom is not about less precision, it’s about more precision. I’m creating my own rules and they’re much more stringent.” And Anthony Braxton, who I have not interviewed but I read this, he said, “I was never interested in runaway improvisation.”

I understand that quite well. I like to have, if it’s quote unquote free improvisation, whatever that means – I like to have the settings where it’s still I don’t want to say controlled like but I kind of am controlling it as a composer setting up a certain structure or guidelines for in the moment in which if I’m recording a series of improvisations they might be pretty short. So right there I might have, especially on the new things that I just did recently when I got a sabbatical and I was on the East Coast…

dear old friends and many new friends, and we would – we recorded many two-minute tracks. They were free but they were lots of little miniatures. And then the end product I would, with my decisions, put them together in interesting sequences basically. But when something is only two minutes you really just grab on to one or two ideas and let it be. If you want something to be totally free but 15, 18, 20 minutes, you better have, as Karl kind of was saying, and/or Braxton, some serious ideas up in your sleeve that…
